title: Safe Guidelines Based on International Consensus
summary:
This chapter turns the international consensus into practical safety guidance. Controlled, adapted exercise is safe and beneficial for mother and fetus, with 150 min of moderate activity per week spread over at least three sessions, preferably daily. It covers special populations, recommended exercise types, how to adapt by trimester, and when to stop a session or the whole program.

Low-intensity exercise in controlled gestational diabetes or mild hypertension improves metabolic control under multidisciplinary supervision, and in obesity, exercise plus nutritional counselling reduces weight gain and macrosomia risk. Tables list warning signs that mean stopping immediately, absolute contraindications (such as severe preeclampsia or placenta praevia with bleeding) and relative ones (such as moderate anemia or multiple pregnancy). Resuming requires gradual progression and obstetrician authorization.
points: The consensus is 150 min of moderate activity per week, spread over at least three sessions per week, preferably daily.
Suggested frequency is 3-5 days per week, at moderate intensity (12-14 on the Borg scale or the talk test), in 30-55-min sessions.
Inactive women should start gradually with 10-15 min daily, while previously active women can keep vigorous training under professional supervision.
Recommended activities include walking, swimming, stationary cycling, gentle jogging, light dancing, bands or light weights, prenatal yoga and adapted Pilates.
Avoid impact, risk of falling or abdominal trauma, for example contact sports, horse riding or skiing.

By trimester: first, progressive adaptation and pelvic floor; second, avoid supine exercise and work lumbar-pelvic stability; third, reduce impact and intensity and favor aquatic or low-impact exercise.
Stop a session immediately for severe dyspnea, chest pain, dizziness, vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, regular contractions, persistent abdominal pain or a sudden decrease in fetal movements.
Absolute contraindications include severe preeclampsia (hypertension >=160/110 mmHg), placenta previa with active bleeding (>26 weeks), PROM and severe anemia (Hb < 9 g/dL).
Relative contraindications include moderate anemia (Hb 9-11 g/dL), uncontrolled diabetes, BMI > 40 or < 18.5, and multiple pregnancy at risk of preterm delivery.
takeaways: Use the talk test: you should be able to hold a fluent conversation without shortness of breath.
Start with 10-15 min daily if you were inactive, and build up gradually.
Drink water before, during and after exercise and avoid hot environments.
Choose low-impact or aquatic options as the third trimester advances.
Keep activity logs and regular medical monitoring alongside education.
After a problem resolves, resume at low intensity and short duration, with obstetrician approval.
cautions: If a warning sign appears, stop immediately, adopt a semi-sitting or left side lying position, hydrate and report to a healthcare professional; get urgent obstetric evaluation if symptoms persist.
Avoid prolonged supine positioning in the second and third trimesters, as it can reduce venous return and cause maternal hypotension.
With absolute contraindications, suspend exercise completely until medical resolution.
